content.title: Where to watch the Chicago River dye: Best spots to see the annual tradition
content.text: While the annual river dye can be seen from several locations in the city, there are some spots that are better than others. You’re watching the NBC 5 Chicago News streaming channel, which plays local Chicago news 24 hours a day, seven days a week. You can find the “NBC 5 Chicago News” streaming channel on your phone or computer, and on Peacock, Samsung, Roku, Xumo or on our app, so you can watch our local news on your schedule. NOTE: NBC Chicago will offer a live stream of the festivities beginning at 10 a.m. Saturday here. It’s about that time! Chicago’s river will turn green Saturday in one of the city’s most beloved annual traditions. The weather is predicted to be in the 30s – not warm, but nothing Chicagoans can’t handle – so expect large crowds descending on downtown. While the river dye can be seen from several locations in the city, there are some spots that are better than others. The best spot to watch is between Michigan Avenue and Columbus Drive. Many people also choose to line up along upper Wacker drive. The State Street bridge is closed this year, so that’s one less vantage point for viewers. Local The river dyeing starts at 10 a.m. Saturday. City officials recommend arriving early to secure your spot to see the Plumbers Union Local 130 do the dyeing. Watch for a lead boat and a chase boat. In the boat, you’ll notice the people are wearing white suits but are covered in orange. The dye is actually orange in color, but when it hits the water it turns bright emerald green. And if you aren't able to make it in person to catch the festivities, you'll still be able to watch it live from home. NBC Chicago will offer a live feed of the event starting at 10 a.m. here.
